_comment: Editorial content for the published matrix. Kept out of tools/artifact_matrix.py so a CI run never needs a source edit to say what a run found, and so the findings list can be reviewed as prose rather than as Python.
title: VISA Conformance Matrix
lede: Spec-cited conformance checks over HiSLIP and VXI-11, run from one container against one fault-injecting mock server. Rows where the implementations disagree carry colour. Click any row with a caret for the full failure or skip detail.

findings.text: a termination character of 0x1FF is stored as 511; both vendors mask it to a byte
a 300-character shared-lock key is accepted, where 256 or more is an error
a nested exclusive lock is not reported; over VXI-11 the session waits out its own timeout against a lock it already holds
an unlock that leaves a lock still held is not reported
VI_SUSPEND_HNDLR | VI_HNDLR is accepted; the modes are mutually exclusive
the resource class suffix is matched case-sensitively — ::instr is refused where ::INSTR opens
four required message-based attributes are missing
required operations raise a Python exception instead of returning a status
a maxRecvSize of zero wedges the session — viWrite never returns
a stalled connection answers VI_ERROR_IO about 11 s late; NI-VISA answers VI_ERROR_TSK_TIMEOUT at 2001 ms

vendor_findings.text: viWaitOnEvent does not dequeue an event whose type was disabled after it arrived
shared locks over HiSLIP are refused outright with VI_ERROR_INV_PROTOCOL
VI_ATTR_TRIG_ID is required of every INSTR resource and supported by none of them on TCPIP

footer: Skips are counted and coloured separately from passes throughout. A skipped check reads like a passing one at a glance, and the ones that matter are those that stay skipped run after run — so every skip carries its reason.
